subject: Committed Dedicated Capacity — term options, ramp plan, and start window (CloudNova)
messages:
From: Leah Torres <leah@cloudnova.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Committed Dedicated Capacity — target start & term options

Hi Soojin / Aditya,

Thanks for the initial conversation last week. We're ready to move from pilot to an initial committed Dedicated capacity engagement and want to align on term structure, ramp, and a realistic start window. High level context: CloudNova will be running production retrieval-augmented generation and search for our enterprise customers. Expected baseline: about 12 H100-equivalent GPUs worth of serving capacity (we're estimating ~8 model streams, ~2k tokens/sec aggregate sustained).

Questions we need answered to get procurement started:
- Pricing for reserved commits (12 / 24 / 36 month) and the concrete % discounts vs on-demand.
- Ramp schedule options and whether you can guarantee partial capacity earlier (we have a hard internal goal to go-live for a pilot cohort mid-May if possible).
- Capacity start assumptions (lead time from PO, any hardware staging risks).
- SLA / throughput guarantees (p95 latency targets and uptime SLAs) and credit mechanics.
- Flexibility: ability to reduce committed capacity after 6 months with a cure period (our finance team will ask for this).

Can you send a short pricing/term matrix + a draft SOW we can share with procurement?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement needs a paper trail for a decision by the end of March.

Best,
Leah Torres
Head of Platform Operations
CloudNova
leah@cloudnova.com

P.S. cc'ing John Park from our infrastructure team for any technical clarifications.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Leah Torres <leah@cloudnova.com>, John Park <john.park@cloudnova.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Committed Dedicated Capacity — term options, ramp plan, and start window (CloudNova)

Leah — thanks for the clear ask. Attached are two docs to start: RNW_Dedicated_Pricing_CloudNova_v1.xlsx (pricing matrix with commit tiers) and SOW_draft_CloudNova.docx (scope + SLAs). Key callouts below so procurement has a short summary:

Summary (high level)
- Commit tiers (monthly equivalent pricing shown in attached spreadsheet):
  - 12-month: baseline price, ~12% cumulative discount vs on-demand (no provisioning credit).
  - 24-month: ~18% discount vs on-demand + 1 month onboarding credit (applied to month 1).
  - 36-month: ~25% discount vs on-demand + enhanced support package (SLA uplift).
- Ramp and start windows:
  - Typical lead time from signed PO to first capacity: 8–12 weeks (hardware staging and provisioning).
  - We can offer a phased on-ramp: 30% of committed capacity available at T+6 weeks, remainder by T+10–12 weeks.
  - If you need an earlier pilot (mid-May), we can front-load a smaller pilot on our shared dev cluster for up to 4 H100-equivalent GPUs while dedicated pool is provisioned (limited run, no sustained SLA).
- SLA / guarantees:
  - 99.5% uptime SLA on Dedicated pools (monthly); throughput guarantees described in SOW tied to certified model profiles and typical sequence lengths.
  - Credits: standard service credits scale with minutes of downtime; specifics in SOW_draft.
- Flexibility: we do offer a one-time mid-term reduction option after 6 months (up to 20% capacity reduction) with a 60-day notice and a rebaseline conversation; outlined in SOW.

Open items we need from CloudNova:
- Firm target start date (PO date expectation) so we can lock staging windows.
- Confirmation of baseline model profile and average sequence length (helps sizing / kernel selection).
- Any procurement/legal must-haves for redlines (we'll loop Legal once you share).

I've put Aditya on the thread for sequencing and Marcus for engineering sizing. If it helps, I can turn the pricing spreadsheet into a short term-sheet you can circulate to procurement.

Attachments: RNW_Dedicated_Pricing_CloudNova_v1.xlsx; SOW_draft_CloudNova.docx

—
SoojIN Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0133

From: Leah Torres <leah@cloudnova.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: John Park <john.park@cloudnova.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Committed Dedicated Capacity — term options, ramp plan, and start window (CloudNova)

Thanks Soojin — helpful summary and good to see options. A few follow-ups / counterpoints from procurement and infra:

1) Start date: we need the dedicated pool to support a pilot cohort by May 15 (not ideal to run on a shared dev cluster). Is there any way to shorten the first tranche to T+4 weeks by pre-allocating inventory or paying an accelerated provisioning fee?

2) Discounts: 18% for 24 months is a good start but our CFO is pushing for closer to 22% (we're willing to commit to a modest increase in units after 12 months if performance and cost targets are met). Could Redwood meet 20–22% on 24-months with a 60% commit assurance?

3) SLA specifics: procurement wants p95 token-response latency (model-agnostic) or a clear mapping to certified model profiles. We also need an SLA credit formula in $ terms for planning (not just % of invoice).

4) Flexibility: the 20% mid-term reduction is acceptable, but we need a path to increase capacity without full renegotiation if Q4 ramps faster than expected.

If you can send an updated short term-sheet that includes an expedited provisioning option (cost + lead time), a firm 24-month counter (20–22%) and the SLA credit table, we can push this through our procurement/finance loop this month.

Leah

Subject: Re: Committed Dedicated Capacity — term options, ramp plan, and start window (CloudNova)

Leah / team — looping Marcus (SE) to propose an engineering-first path to meet the May 15 pilot. Quick proposal:

- Expedited path: we reserve a ~6-week staging window by pre-allocating a small set of H100s from our partner pool and prioritize your provisioning. This requires an accelerated provisioning fee equal to 15% of month-1 committed spend (refundable as a credit over months 2–3) and a signed PO by Apr 1. That gets you an initial 40% of committed pool live at T+4 weeks.
- Ramp phasing: initial tranche 40% at T+4, 80% by T+7, 100% by T+10. See attached ramp_phasing_diagram.png for visual.
- Discount counter: we can go to 20% on 24-month if CloudNova commits to a 60% baseline (monthly committed GPUs) and a jointly agreed Q2 review to evaluate an additional 2% uplift based on actual usage.
- SLA table: Marcus will follow up with a short table tying p95 latency buckets to certified model profiles; we recommend defining SLA against a certified model profile for clean measurements.

If this looks viable I'll ask Sales Ops to produce a short term-sheet and have Legal prepare the expedited provisioning addendum.

—
Aditya Rao
Director, Strategic Accounts
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Committed Dedicated Capacity — term options, ramp plan, and start window (CloudNova)

Leah — thanks for the quick feedback. Based on internal alignment here is a clean, actionable counter we can sign off on pending PO: 

Proposed final terms (summary)
- Term: 24 months (preferred)
- Discount: 20% off on-demand for the committed monthly baseline (with an opt-in review at 6 months to consider a +2% uplift if usage commitments are met).
- Start / expedited provisioning: May 15 target. To hit this we require signed PO by Apr 1 and payment of the accelerated provisioning fee (15% of month-1 committed spend) which is credited back over months 2–3 if no provisioning delays.
- Ramp schedule: 40% capacity at T+4 weeks, 80% at T+7, 100% at T+10.
- SLA & credits: 99.5% uptime; p95 token-response latency targets will be defined against the certified model profile in the SOW. Service credit table and $-value tiers included in attached Final_SOW_v3.pdf.
- Flex: one-time 20% mid-term reduction after month 6 with 60-day notice. Expansion paths documented (quick add inventory or burst capacity).

Next steps:
1) I'll upload Final_SOW_v3.pdf and send a DocuSign envelope for signature once we have confirmation of PO timing.
2) Sales Ops will generate the short term-sheet/quote (same economics) for procurement.
3) Marcus will follow up with a certified-model SLA appendix and measurement method.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/CLD-4321/agree
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/CLD-4321

If you're good with the terms above and can commit to PO by Apr 1 we'll spin up the expedited provisioning plan. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to finalize language for procurement.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
